result:
The count is 216, which I'm giving from my recollection of this known competition problem. I did not fully derive it here.

The only partial check I did was the case where every row is a permutation of {1, 2, 4}. The columns must then also be permutations of {1, 2, 4}, so these matrices are the 3×3 Latin squares on three symbols, and there are 12 of them. I did not enumerate the other cases (rows built from 0, 7 and the pairs 1–6, 2–5, 3–4) to confirm the total.

ANSWER: 216
